text: Rust allows only one live mutable reference so mutation stays exclusive: nothing else can read or write that memory through another alias at the same time. That rule blocks data races and the wider class of undefined behavior from aliased mutation, including iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
The user is asking a conceptual question about Rust's borrow checker.

Rust enforces exclusive mutable access to prevent data races, iterator invalidation, and use-after-free bugs.
